notes: 1916 four-storey flats. Colour taken from the blur (warm taupe-brown), everything else is the block's 1910s pattern: painted stucco, two cant bays from storey 1 to the roof, a bracketed cornice, a centre stair entry and one garage door at street level. Wall darkened toward the blur's medium warm brown-taupe, the rest stays the block fallback. Medium-dark brown stucco with dark brown trim, frames, cornice brackets and shop frames; the white roll-up garage and plain door are replaced by two large dark-framed ground windows either side of a centre stair entry under a brown canvas awning with a valance; the small light-well jogs on the side (edges 1, 5, 6, 7) are treated as blind party returns so no sills or hoods float in the notches. Wall re-tinted toward the blur's mauve grey-brown (6f5c58). Geometry unchanged (shopfront/hood claims unverifiable either way). SvS shows a brown corner building whose awning/bays match 262707054 (identity doubt), so only colours applied: medium brown 7a5f52, dark brown trim 4e3a30, dark awning 3e2a22. Geometry unchanged, no basement band (no key/verified). Tint lift (2026-10-02): wall tints lifted toward the sunlit paint (t' = 1-(1-t)k).
